trigger: a server upgrade whose installed_software table holds about 4 million rows (roughly 13,000 agents at 300 rows each): the first draft of migration v7 spent 32.3 s in one ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN install_id BIGSERIAL (a full rewrite that also rebuilt both existing indexes), over the pool's 30 s per-statement limit
classification_rationale: the ladder note and the migration comment called the rewrite 'bounded' and 'about 0.5 s on 200k rows' and an early estimate put the limit at 12-19M rows; measured at 4M rows the committed SQL was cancelled at boot (fail-closed); the boot failure is loud and diagnosable (fail-closed), so it is unavailability at upgrade, not harmful guidance that conceals state
summary: Migration v7 as first written would be cancelled by the 30 s statement limit at about 4M rows and the server would refuse to boot. Reported independently by unhappy-path (762 MB / ~4M), enterprise-readiness (29.2 s at 4M) and sre (3-8M); the orchestrator reproduced it (32.3 s rewrite + 21.2 s index at 4M rows). Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091: the old name index is dropped before the column add and the limit is lifted for that migration's transaction only; the same SQL then took about 4 s + 6.5 s at 4M rows under a 30 s session limit and re-ran idempotently. Ladder, manual and changelog corrected.

trigger: two replicas start together on the first boot after upgrade: the loser waits on the migration advisory lock under a 10 s lock timeout while the winner rewrites the table, then refuses to start; a long reader ahead of the exclusive ALTER also queues later queries
classification_rationale: the operational consequence of new exclusive DDL on a live table was undocumented (required-doc item 2)
summary: First-start races around the new exclusive-lock migration were undocumented. No code change (any lock handling change in the runner is a new surface). Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091 as documentation: start one replica first and let the migration finish; avoid long readers during that first start.

trigger: an operator upgrades a server with a large existing inventory and finds nothing telling them the first start rewrites the table or how long it takes
classification_rationale: required-doc item 2: a docs/user-manual section for a changed upgrade step; the changelog carried only the deploy-order sentence
summary: No operator upgrade note for the one-time table rewrite and the deploy order. Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091: an Upgrading paragraph in docs/user-manual/inventory.md and a matching clause in the changelog fragment.

trigger: a future reviewer relying on the routed-concern row reads 'blob v2's 12-field order is hashed byte-identically' and does not learn about the conditional 4-field tail rule that now exists only in code
classification_rationale: the row states a field count that the hash contract no longer matches; required-doc items 4 and 6 (routed-concern row named as an update obligation for the changed surface)
summary: Routed-concern row 38 clause (4) still described a 12-field hash contract. Reported independently by docs-writer, consistency-auditor and architect. Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091: the clause now states 12 fields plus the 4-field tail appended (all four) only when any is non-empty, with the agent mirror pending.

trigger: an operator reads the manual's statement that install_location sits outside the daily sync, next to the schema listing that shows the column in the synced table; no agent populates the column yet, so no wrong outcome occurs today
classification_rationale: the manual's data-handling sentence and the new schema listing disagree; E6 caps it at LOW because the column stays empty until an agent emits it
summary: Manual says install_location is outside the sync while the synced table now has the column; also 'every column except agent_id and name may be empty' was false for install_id. Reported independently by compliance-officer, docs-writer, security-guardian and consistency-auditor. Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091 (manual only; the privacy paragraph stays factual, no classification claim). The ADR's older note is deliberately not edited (owner decision).

trigger: a reader trusts the comment above the batched INSERT ('four parallel arrays, constant 5 params') or the header claims that the agent's builder walks the full field sequence
classification_rationale: the comments contradict the code (16 arrays, 17 parameters; the agent builder still emits 12 fields); adjacent to changed lines, comment-only
summary: Stale comments near the batched INSERT and in the header. Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091 (comment-only).

trigger: a mutant that drops install_id from the paging order still passes because ids are monotone with insertion; an unbounded walk loop would hang on a non-advancing cursor; a pin comment claimed more than it pinned
classification_rationale: a test comment claimed to pin the whole tail comparison chain but pins only the source arm; missing coverage of bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a floor
summary: Keyset test could not pin the install_id tiebreak, the walk loop had no page cap, and one pin comment overclaimed. Fixed in the governance-round commit 818b85091: the test now bumps one id out of insertion order and asserts the walk follows it, the loop is capped with a REQUIRE, and the comment states what it pins.

trigger: the server is rolled back while agents that emit the extended fields are deployed, or an agent emits a 16-field record with an all-empty tail, or emits a 17th field: the stored 12- or 16-field re-serialisation differs from the agent's own blob hash and it resends every cycle
classification_rationale: the agent-side mirror of the tail rule does not exist yet and is deliberately out of this change; the behaviour is the documented inherited mixed-version property
summary: Agent-side contract items (mirror the tail rule, comment at the agent builder now stale, rollback caveat, possible 'trim trailing empties' alternative, privacy paragraph once install_location is emitted) belong to the agent change. Would-be issue drafted in the run report; not filed because no push or PR exists yet.
disposition: deferred-to-issue #TBD (draft in the run report; to be filed when the PR is raised)

trigger: a reader meets installed_software.source (the plugin action that produced a row) and inventory_state.source (the sync-source key) in one schema
classification_rationale: a naming observation; the two columns live in different tables and mean different things
summary: New column name 'source' echoes the sync-source key elsewhere in the schema. Rejected: the name is fixed by the approved plan; flagged to the owner as cheapest to change before an agent hard-codes it.

trigger: two rows for one agent differ only in the new fields; the per-agent read orders by name and version
classification_rationale: no prose involved; a behaviour note about an existing tie order (rows differing only in other v2 fields already tied)
summary: The per-agent read has no tiebreak for rows differing only in the appended fields. Rejected as pre-existing behaviour of a per-device list that is not a paged cursor.

trigger: two local commit subjects named internal review steps and were non-conventional
classification_rationale: commit-message wording; conventional subjects are the house style, but history is preserved as committed by the owner's standing rule
summary: Three local gate-fix commit subjects (482467700, 52a14af9c, 818b85091) name internal review steps and are non-conventional. Not fixed: the owner ruled on 2026-09-29 that commits are never squashed or rewritten, so the subjects stay as committed; a reword would need the owner's explicit request.
